channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: NVIDIA CEO Impressed by Kazakhstan's AI Film Initiatives
item.description: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang expressed admiration for Kazakhstan's plans in AI film development, particularly the Astana AI Film Festival. He suggested Kazakhstan could become a major hub for AI cinema, comparable to Cannes. Freedom Holding Corp., through its "Freedom Shafagat" foundation, sponsored the festival with $1 million in prizes.

item.title: Tajikistan and Uzbekistan Exchange Water Resource Management Experience
item.description: Specialists from Uzbekistan's Ministry of Water Resources and women members of the Zerafshan River Basin Council visited Tajikistan from October 21-23, 2026, to study integrated water resource management. They explored experiences with the Kofarnihon River Basin Council and Women's Forum, focusing on rational use and women's participation.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish Full-Cycle Drone Production and Test Autonomous Freight
item.description: Kazakhstan has approved a comprehensive plan for 2026-2029 to develop a full cycle of drone production, including vertiports and charging stations. In 2027-2028, a pilot project for autonomous freight transport will be launched. The initiative aims to foster sovereign production from hardware to software, offering state support and incentives for competitive enterprises.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Congratulates Healthcare and Pharmaceutical Workers on Professional Holiday
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated healthcare and pharmaceutical workers on their professional holiday, highlighting achievements over the past decade. He noted a threefold increase in medical services and the launch of new pharmaceutical facilities worth $1 billion.

item.title: Alatau to Construct Skyscraper Complex Worth Over 360 Billion Tenge
item.description: Construction has begun on Alatau's first skyscraper, a 272-meter-high structure part of the Iconic Complex. The project, involving two towers (272m and 78m), will house offices, residences, a hotel, and commercial spaces, with completion planned by the end of 2029. Over 360.8 billion tenge will be invested.

item.title: Kazakhstan Revokes Licenses of Seven Microfinance Organizations for Legal Violations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market has revoked the licenses of seven microfinance organizations (MFOs) for systematic violations of legal requirements. The affected MFOs must re-register or decide on liquidation within 30 days, removing references to microfinance from their names. This action follows previous measures against financial institutions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Pursues Direct Flights to EU Countries, Eyes China Route
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is actively working towards establishing direct flights to European Union countries, according to the Director of the Civil Aviation Agency. The agency is in talks with EU airlines and Chinese carriers to facilitate new routes. Domestic airline Asman Airlines expects delivery of two Airbus A321 aircraft by late 2027, capable of direct EU flights.

item.title: Tajikistan President Proposes New Head for Election Commission Ahead of 2027 Polls
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon of Tajikistan has proposed replacing the head of the Central Election Commission (CEC). Zarif Alizoda, a former legal advisor, has been nominated for the position. This initiative comes ahead of the presidential elections expected in 2027. The current CEC head, Bakhtiyor Khudoyorzoda, who has led the commission since 2016, is also proposed for removal.

item.title: Iran's Embassies Delete Posts on Samarkand Heritage After Uzbekistan's Protest
item.description: Iran's embassies in Armenia, China, and Zimbabwe have removed social media posts concerning Samarkand's historical and cultural heritage following a strong protest from Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Uzbekistan had summoned Iran's ambassador, Muhammad Ali Iskandariy, on October 23rd, demanding the removal of posts that claimed Samarkand's heritage as part of Persian civilization.

item.title: Seven Microfinance Organizations Lose Licenses in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market has revoked the licenses of seven microfinance organizations (MFOs) following inspections that revealed systematic violations of consumer rights and legislation. The revoked licenses belong to MaxMoney, Microfinance Systems, SurfKaz Finance, MFO№1, 'Umit Finance', 'Vivus', and EL QAZYNA. MFOs are required to re-register or liquidate within 30 days.

item.title: Major Crypto Platform Kraken Enters Kazakhstan's Digital Asset Market
item.description: International crypto platform Kraken is entering Kazakhstan's digital asset market. The Ministry of Digital Development and Kraken signed a memorandum of cooperation, aiming to develop the digital asset market and implement blockchain technologies in Kazakhstan. Kraken received preliminary approval from the Astana Financial Services Authority (AFSA).

item.title: Tajikistan and Qatar Discuss Trade, Investment, and Rogun Dam Financing
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Economic Development and Trade met with Qatar's Minister of State for Foreign Trade in Doha to discuss expanding economic, trade, and investment cooperation. Special attention was given to financing the Rogun Dam project and increasing Tajik agricultural exports to Qatar. They also explored direct flights and an entrepreneur forum.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Acknowledges Ineffectiveness of Prison Sentences for Alimony Non-Payment
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov stated that stricter penalties for alimony non-payment do not guarantee debt recovery and can hinder debtors' ability to earn. The government will further study changes to criminal and administrative sanctions to ensure alimony obligations are met. The PM also noted that expanding housing subsidies is not feasible due to budget constraints.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy in 2027: Analysts Predict Tenge Depreciation Amidst Lower Oil Prices and Interest Rates
item.description: Analysts forecast that Kazakhstan's tenge may weaken against the US dollar by 2027, reaching 515 tenge per dollar. This projection is based on the gradual decrease in the base interest rate and potential decline in oil prices. While the tenge strengthened in Q3 2023, future factors like reduced National Bank currency supply and lower rates are expected to influence its course.

item.title: UAE to Fund Construction of Homes for Nearly 3,000 Afghan Returnees
item.description: The United Arab Emirates has signed a $3 million agreement with UNHCR to build permanent homes for approximately 2,950 Afghan returnees. The project, announced at AidEx 2026, will focus on providing sustainable shelter in Kabul, Herat, and Kunduz provinces, with a special emphasis on supporting vulnerable women and children affected by humanitarian crises.

item.title: Azerbaijani Company May Conduct Exploration at Kashkadarya Gold Mine
item.description: An Azerbaijani company has registered its first foreign subsidiary in Uzbekistan and may conduct exploration activities at the Akba gold mine in the Kashkadarya region. Following the acquisition of a license, the company plans to commence 18 months of geological exploration work at the site.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Reportedly Deports Critics on Private Jets at Significant Cost
item.description: Reports indicate that Kyrgyzstan is using private jets to deport critics of the government, incurring costs of millions of soms. This practice involves flying individuals out of the country on expensive charter flights. The details suggest a significant expenditure of public funds for the removal of dissenting voices.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Detains Seven in International Drug Trafficking Ring Bust
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNB) has dismantled two international drug trafficking groups suspected of supplying synthetic drugs from CIS countries. Seven Kyrgyz citizens were arrested in Bishkek with over 3.5 million soms worth of alpha-PVP seized. Criminal cases have been initiated under Article 282 of the Criminal Code.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Two Former Officials Detained for Corruption Moved to House Arrest
item.description: Former Kyrgyz Minister of Health, Kanybek Dosmambetov, and ex-deputy head of the State Committee for National Security, Kurvanbek Avazov, have been moved from pre-trial detention to house arrest. A Bishkek court approved the change in pre-trial measures, suspecting them of receiving large bribes and abuse of power.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Tighten Oversight of Private Bailiffs, Introduce New Licensing Rules
item.description: Kazakhstan is enhancing control over private bailiffs (ChSI) by introducing new grounds for license suspension and mandatory triennial attestation for all active bailiffs starting January 1, 2027. Failure to pass this attestation or address identified violations may lead to license revocation, according to Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov.

item.title: Kazakhstan Detains 537 Individuals Wanted by Other Countries
item.description: Over the first nine months of 2026, Kazakhstan police apprehended 537 individuals sought by CIS and foreign countries, in addition to over 17,000 missing persons located. Among those detained were suspects in fraud cases, including one accused of defrauding over 401 million tenge in 2018 and another of over 1.3 billion tenge in 2023.

item.title: Kazakhstan President to Visit Turkey for Official Engagement
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev will undertake an official visit to Turkey this week, as announced by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The visit coincides with Turkey's Republic Day celebrations and the 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS), themed 'Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought, and Deeds'.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Reform Film Industry, Abolish State Orders
item.description: Uzbekistan is restructuring its film industry, abolishing the state order system for film production. The state-owned "O'zbekfilm" will be dissolved and replaced by a national film company focused on developing a national film brand and modernizing the industry. The private sector will take full responsibility for film creation, with the new company handling project selection, financing, promotion, and distribution.

item.title: Families of 68 Children Who Died in Uzbekistan Receive Compensation After Four Years
item.description: Families of 68 children who died in Uzbekistan after taking 'Dok-1 Max' and 'Ambronol' syrups have finally received full compensation after four years. 20% of the funds were recovered from convicted individuals, while the state covered the remaining 80%, according to Egemen.kz.

item.title: Online Taxation: Fewer Reports, More Payments in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, the online taxpayer portal has seen a significant increase in tax payments, reaching 25.4 billion soms in the incomplete 2026 year, a nineteen-fold increase from 2024. Concurrently, the number of submitted reports has decreased substantially. This shift is attributed to the evolution and increased functionality of the digital service, designed to simplify tax procedures and reduce taxpayer burden.

item.title: Temporary Ceasefire in Aloshky for Humanitarian Operation Takes Effect
item.description: A temporary ceasefire has been implemented in the Aloshky area of Kherson region starting October 27, 2026, to facilitate a humanitarian operation. The aim is to deliver aid to residents and prepare for civilian evacuation. Both the Ukrainian General Staff and the Russian Ministry of Defense confirmed the ceasefire, with Russia ceasing fire from 04:00 Moscow time and Ukraine from 03:00 Kyiv time.

item.title: Tornado Hits Antalya, Turkey, Causing Fatalities and Injuries
item.description: A tornado struck Antalya, Turkey, resulting in four deaths and one injury. The twister formed at a construction site in the Kepez district, overturning containers where five workers were present. Two workers died at the scene, and two more succumbed to their injuries in the hospital. The fifth worker sustained minor injuries. Authorities are continuing to survey the area.

item.title: Tajikistan and China begin construction of new road infrastructure in Dushanbe
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon and Dushanbe's Mayor laid the foundation stone for the construction of overpasses and a bridge on Sherozi Avenue. This project, part of cooperation with China's international development agency, follows the commencement of construction on three overpasses and a bridge on Abdulahad Kaharov Street earlier in October.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates Billions from Waste Fees for Environmental Projects
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources has allocated 122.6 billion tenge from waste collection fees to fund 34 environmental projects. These projects include building new recycling facilities, creating sorting complexes, and acquiring specialized equipment.

item.title: Seven Microfinance Organizations in Kazakhstan Lose Licenses
item.description: Seven microfinance organizations in Kazakhstan have had their licenses revoked due to violations of consumer rights. The Financial Regulation and Development Agency stated these measures aim to prevent unfair practices and ensure compliance with legal requirements.

item.title: US Reportedly Planning to Deport Afghan Refugees from Pakistan
item.description: A report by Bloomberg suggests the United States is planning to deport Afghan refugees currently residing in Pakistan. The details of the plan and its potential implications for the refugees remain unclear.

item.title: Tashkent Apartment Fire Shows Signs of Arson, Homicide Investigation Launched
item.description: An investigation has been launched into a fatal fire in a Tashkent apartment complex that resulted in the death of a 26-year-old woman. Investigators discovered three separate ignition points, indicating possible arson.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates Over 122 Billion Tenge for Waste Recycling Projects
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Ecology reports that over 122 billion tenge from waste collection fees have been allocated to fund 34 projects focused on waste processing, sorting facilities, and specialized equipment.

item.title: Uzbekistan Committee Proposes Digital Control Over Sales Promotions and Discounts
item.description: The Committee for the Development of Competition and Protection of Consumer Rights in Uzbekistan is developing new digital mechanisms to strengthen control over sales promotions and discounts. The proposal includes scanning QR codes to verify previous prices and discount amounts, and registering promotion terms in an electronic system. The goal is to increase transparency and protect consumers from misleading practices.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Investigation into Religious Leader Accused of Abusing Minors
item.description: Kazakhstan has initiated a pre-trial investigation into a religious community led by Ismatulla Maqsum following allegations of sexual abuse against minors. Former followers have spoken out, claiming the religious leader threatened children with imprisonment if they revealed the abuse. The Ministry of Internal Affairs is conducting the investigation, stating that further details cannot be disclosed under Article 201 of the Criminal Procedure Code.

item.title: Mother Alleges Political Prisoner Beaten in Atyrau Colony Toilet
item.description: The mother of political prisoner Gulnaz Serikbaeva has alleged that her daughter was beaten in a toilet at the colony in Atyrau. The details of the alleged assault have not been released, but the mother's statement has raised concerns about the treatment of political prisoners.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates Funds for Maslikhat Election Candidates
item.description: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission has announced the funding for candidates in the upcoming Maslikhat elections. Candidates for regional and city councils will receive between 500,000 and 700,000 tenge for campaign expenses, including media appearances and promotional materials. District council candidates will receive 500,000 tenge.

item.title: Perfectum's Tashkent Real Estate and Assets to be Sold for Nearly 100 Billion Soums
item.description: Shareholders of the mobile operator Perfectum have approved a deal to sell the company's real estate complex in Tashkent's Mirobod district and over two thousand other assets to entrepreneur Oybek Tursunov for nearly 100 billion soums.

item.title: US Reportedly Plans to Deport Afghan Asylum Seekers to Pakistan
item.description: Bloomberg reports that the United States is planning to deport some Afghan asylum seekers to Pakistan. Detained Afghans have been informed of potential transfers in the coming weeks. This plan affects relatives of those who aided the US military. An organization assisting Afghans has documented at least 30 reports of possible transfers.

item.title: Uzbek President's Son-in-Law Acquires Tashkent Real Estate and $8.2 Million in Assets
item.description: Oybek Tursunov, son-in-law of Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, is purchasing real estate and other assets of mobile operator Perfectum for approximately $8.2 million. The deal, approved by shareholders of Rubicon Wireless Communication (Perfectum's brand), includes properties in central Tashkent and 2012 units of fixed assets. The sale was approved shortly before VEON announced its acquisition of Perfectum.
